items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the civil service law, in relation to employee representation
of state employees designated managerial or confidential; and to repeal
certain provisions of such law relating thereto
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2394

SPONSOR: JACKSON
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the civil service law, in relation to employee represen-
tation of state employees designated managerial or confidential; and to
repeal certain provisions of such law relating thereto

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to provide that any state employee desig-
nated managerial or confidential receive certain protections comparable
to union-represented employees under the Taylor Law.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends Section 204 of the Civil Service Law to provide that an
organization representing management/confidential (M/C) employees be
granted certain recognitions under Article 14 of Civil Service Law (also
known as the Taylor Law).

Section 2 repeals Section 214 of the Civil Service law which prohibits
M/Cs from holding membership in an organization seeking certification or
recognition under the Taylor Law.

Section 3 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The rights and privileges afforded recognized and certified employee
organizations under Article 14 of the NYS Civil Service Law are consid-
erable. While Article 14, also known as the Public Employees Fair
Employment Act or the Taylor Law, specifically excludes employees desig-
nated as either "managerial" or "confidential" from organizing for
purposes of collective negotiations, such employees have formed volun-
tary associations to mutually address workplace issues, defend employee
rights, and offer group benefit programs. For managerial or confidential
employees of the state of New York, the Organization of New York State
Management Confidential Employees (OMCE) has been the sole association
for more than 40 years. OMCE works with the Governor's Office of Employ-
ee Relations (GOER) to ensure that managerial or confidential employees
have a voice in state government and are treated no worse than their
union-represented coworkers.

In seeking treatment comparable to that of "recognized and certified"
employee organizations with the express exclusion of collective negoti-
ations, the legislation seeks to formalize the existing relationship
that OMCE enjoys with New York State. This tòitl would allow OMCE to
continue to collect certain membership information and receive automatic
payroll dues deductions while also allowing them to obtain addresses and
contact information for new employees, access to employees during orien-
tation, distribute organizational materials at the worksite, and meet
with members during the work day for purposes of representation in
administrative matters. In other words, this bill helps provide some
parity between the widely enjoyed rights of unionized state employees
and M/Cs. This bill will allow this critical employee organization to
more effectively represent the needs and interests of non-unionized

employees who nonetheless should be subject to some protections and
privileges under the Taylor Law.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2021-2022: S.5726 - Referred to Civil Service and Pensions/A.6541 -
Referred to Governmental Employees

 
STATE AND LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

AN ACT to amend the civil service law, in relation to employee representation
of state employees designated managerial or confidential
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2394A

SPONSOR: JACKSON
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the civil service law, in relation to employee represen-
tation of state employees designated managerial or confidential

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to provide an organization that advocates
for state employees designated managerial or confidential certain
contact information for new hires and for those promoted or transferred
within state employment.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivision 208 of the Civil Service Law by adding new
subdivision 4-a to provide that an organization advocating for manageri-
al or confidential(M/C) employees be notified, by the employer, of
pertinent contact information for newly hired, promoted and transferred
M/C employees within thirty days; allows, within thirty days, for an
organization advocating for M/Cs to meet with such employees; provides
the ability of organizations advocating for MICs to attend employee
orientations.

Section 2 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2018, New York State amended the Civil Service Law to require public
employers to notify and provide employee organizations certain informa-
tion for newly hired, promoted and transferred employees, as well as the
ability of the employee organizations to meet with such employees and
attend employee orientations. This bill would expand the current law to
include M/C employees and organizations that advocate for M/Cs.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2021-2022: S.5726 - Referred to Civil Service and Pensions/A.6541 -
Referred to Governmental Employees

 
STATE AND LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:  None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
